title: Explain what value-type and reference-type assignment copy, including shared reference fields

rubric.point: Struct assignment copies the field values into a separate struct value.
The Weight fields are independent, so assigning 8 to second.Weight leaves first.Weight at 5.
The Labels reference is copied without cloning the list, so adding express mutates the list initially shared by both structs.
Replacing second.Labels changes only that struct's reference field; first.Labels still refers to the original list.

questions.model:
`second = first` copies every field of the struct. Each struct therefore has its own `Weight` value and its own `Labels` reference field.

Changing `second.Weight` affects only the copied integer. The copied `Labels` reference initially points to the same list as `first.Labels`; the list itself was not copied. Adding `"express"` therefore changes their shared list.

Assigning a new list to `second.Labels` replaces only the reference stored in `second`. `first.Labels` continues to point to the original list containing `"fragile"` and `"express"`.

rubric.point: Class assignment copies the object reference, so primary and backup initially refer to one Meter instance.
Changing backup.Reading mutates that shared instance, so primary observes 25.
The final assignment redirects only backup to a new Meter; primary still refers to the previous instance.

questions.model:
`backup = primary` copies the reference to the existing `Meter`, without copying the object. Both variables initially refer to the same instance, so changing its `Reading` through `backup` is also visible through `primary`.

The final assignment creates another `Meter` and stores its reference in `backup`. It changes which object `backup` refers to. `primary` still refers to the earlier object, whose reading remains `25`.
